Commentary.Commentary: That ends another Test match and another mauling. Bangladesh have simply not been able to answer the short ball challenge and they need to find a solution quickly, with the third Test not far away. Join us from Saturday, March 16, 2019 at 11 am local (2200 GMT, previous night) for all the action from the third and final Test. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Victorious Kiwi skipper, Kane Williamson, says that the shoulder is fine for now. Praises his bowlers for finishing the match within 2 and a half days, in spite of bowling not too well in the first innings. Says that the plan was always to be positive, playing good cricket. Feels that the wicket was very challenging, with Bangladesh bowling well on a green wicket in the first innings but without luck. Williamson adds that he and Taylor were able to capitalize on that and took the game out of reach. On the pitch, Kane says that it is very hard to make an accurate judgement but feels it held up nicely and scoring became easier after spending some time on the wicket. Hopes that Bradley Watling's hamstring injury is not serious and he is fit for the next Test.

Bangladesh captain, Mahmudullah, feels that the team could have done a lot lot better as they are a much better unit than that. Admits that there was help with the new ball but the batsmen could have showed some grit. Hopes to do well in the third Test. Agrees that catching let them down too in this game. On the short ball challenge, Mahmudullah puts it to the individuals as  every player is different. Asks the batsmen to judge themselves how good or bad they are playing the short ball and find ways to tackle it.

ROSS TAYLOR HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH. Taylor says that as a batter it always plays in your mind when you look at a green track. Praises the bowlers for getting a result in 2 and a half days and taking 20 wickets. Says that it was a matter of 30 minutes of survival and himself and Williamson were lucky to get through those. Adds that once that period was over, the margin for error was very less for the bowlers and the batsmen took full toll. On going past Martin Crowe's century tally, Rosco says that he held up a couple of glasses for the great man in honour last night and is honoured to have been able to go past him.

A few dropped catches did not help the tourists' cause as they started falling way behind. Then, those two sessions on Day 4 saw Taylor and Nicholls plunder runs. Rosco went on to score his double hundred and at that stage, an innings defeat script was written. Bangladesh were good with the new ball but could not quite sustain the pressure. Please stay tuned for the presentation...

Just to give you a reminder of what happened in this Test. The first 2 days were washed out without a ball being bowled. And yet, we have had a result in 7 sessions. On a super-green wicket, the Kiwis elected to bowl and dismissed the visitors for 211, with only Tamim providing any resistance with his 74. There too, Boult and Wagner shared most of the wickets, 7 to be precise. Come the reply, the Kiwis were 8/2 but then a massive century stand between Williamson and Taylor put Bangladesh on the back foot.

When it comes to short pitch bowling, does any other name come to your mind apart from Neil Wagner? The lion-hearted fellow took yet another 5-fer, following his 4 in the first innings. He has taken 16 wickets in 4 innings in this series, at an average of 14 and a strike rate of 25.2. Brilliant. Trent Boult helped himself with 4 while the other bowlers, though wicketless, were always dangerous.

The day started with the hosts needing 7 wickets to win and they have wrapped things up in a matter of 33 overs. The plan was certain - bowl short and at the body, terrorize the batsmen's minds and get wickets through lack of patience. Short, short, short - the barricade kept on coming and eventually, the batting succumbed. Shadman, Mithun and Sarkar got starts, but could not quite convert them into big knocks. Mahmudullah easily looked the best of the lot, playing the short balls with ease.
2-0 for New Zealand with a Test to go. Not surprising at all. Yet another game where an Asian side has been bounced out.

OUT! Timber and it is a 5-fer for Wagner! Full and straight. Ebadot backs away, aiming to go through the off side but the ball is too good for him. Goes under his bat and bang. NEW ZEALAND WIN BY AN INNINGS AND 12 RUNS!
A full toss outside off, Ebadot backs away to slash but misses.
Ebadot Hossain is the last man in.

OUT! In the air and taken! No century for the skipper and Bangladesh are still 12 short of avoiding an innings defeat. Not surprisingly, a short ball, around middle, Mahmudullah looks to pull but is cramped for room. Gets a top edge which skies miles in the air. Trent Boult runs to his right from third man and takes it nicely.
A short ball down the leg side, Mahmudullah lets it go.
SIX! That is a terrific shot. Even Wagner admires it. A short ball outside off, Mahmudullah carves it over point and the ball goes all the way! The deficit is now 12.
A length ball around middle, helped towards square leg.
Goes for the yorker to end the over but bowls a full toss instead. The batsman puts his bat down and plays it to extra cover.
Fullish delivery outside off, Abu tries to play and defend it but keeps his bat on the wrong line and misses to connect.

NOT OUT. New Zealand waste a review but they will not care too much about it. They will like to finish this off quickly. A short ball, around middle, Jayed looked to fend it off but missed. The ball went off something, to the naked eye and keeper Bocock appealed. The umpire turned it down and Southee went for the review. Hot Spot showed a mark on the helmet while Snicko showed nothing.
Review for a caught behind! The keeper looks very confident and Southee has obliged.
Abu Jayed walks in at number 10, replacing Mustafizur. LUNCH HAS BEEN EXTENDED BY 15 MINUTES, as 8 wickets are down.

OUT! BOWLED! Straight and full, and that's how it is done. A full length delivery on middle stump and straight. Rahman was going for a big shot but misses it completely. The ball knocks the middle stump out. And that's how one gets a tail-ender. Just 2 wickets more for Kiwis to seal the deal for this Test. Can they finish this off in this session itself?
A well-directed bouncer, ducked by Rahman watchfully.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.

Finally the full ball comes. It is on the stumps and Mustafizur has a massive heave. Mistimes it high in the air but mid off cannot get to it running back. The ball lands safely and strangely, the batsmen are happy with the single.
Pitched outside off angling away, Mustafizur plays the wrong line and the ball goes to the keeper.
Short and outside leg, Rahman tries to play fine but misses to hit.
A replica of the first delivery and the batsman tries the same shot and misses again.
Length delivery outside off, Rahman tries to heave a big shot over mid-wicket but totally plays down the wrong line.
Comes from round the wicket to the left hander, pitches it short on middle. Rahman goes on his knees to play the upper cut but misses to get bat on ball.
A bad delivery pitched outside leg and goes wide. Boult just gets away with it. The umpire gives the FIRST OFFICIAL WARNING TO BOULT for running on the pitch.
FOUR! A good timing shot! A short pitch delivery around off, Mahmudullah goes on the back foot. Using the angle and pace just plays it with precision towards point for a boundary.
A length delivery outside off angling away, Mahmudullah shoulders his arms.
A full length delivery on middle and leg, Rahman makes some room and hits towards mid-wicket for a single.
A short pitch delivery outside off, tempting Mustafizur to play. Rahman almost falls for the trap, attempting an upper cut but misses it.
SIX! Freaky six. A short ball, around middle, Mustafizur looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball flies straight in the  air but well over the keeper and beyond the ropes.
Trent Boult is back on. 14-4-41-3 so far.

A short ball down the leg side, the skipper looks to pull but misses. Wagner smiles and starts to sledge Mahmudullah. He gets something back in return and both players continue to chirp. A watchful Paul Reiffel is observing all and is smiling too. Must have been reminded of his haydays, the former Aussie speedster.

Half tracker near the shoulders, Mahmudullah pulls it away. He gets the elevation but could not get the timing. The fielder at short mid-wicket runs behind and gathers up the ball. The batsman complete a brace.
Mahmudullah stands up on his toes to play this short ball.
Shorter delivery going down leg, the batsman manages to leave it to the keeper.
Changes his line totally, Wagner goes for the blockhole. Mahmudullah manages to dig it out at the last moment.
Back of a length delivery angling away outside off, defended from the back foot.
A loopy full length delivery on leg, Rahman flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Change of angle for Mustifizur. A bouncer, pitched on off and middle, Rahman ducks it.
A short of good length delivery around off, Mahmudullah goes on the back foot and lets the ball come to him, opens the face the bat towards point, adds a run to the scoreboard.
A well-directed bouncer. Pitched on middle, ducked by Mahmudullah.
Back of length on middle, defended under his eyes on the back foot.
A short of length delivery around off, defended easily by Mahmudullah on the back foot.
A bit of a halt in play. Mahmudullah is having some issue with his right shoulder. The physio is out in the middle.
Bouncer to end the over, Rahman defends it from the crease.
LUCKY! Mahmudullah backs away to play the pull on this length ball but gets a thick top edge. The ball skies to the area between mid on and mid off and falls just between them. A single taken.
Full outside off, the batsman tries to drive but misses to put bat on ball.
On a good length around off, the skipper hops to defend but the ball moves away and takes the leading edge. Lands safely on the off side.

FOUR! Fine shot to bring up a fighting half century. Mahmudullah backs away to this short ball and clubs it straight back over the bowler's head. It has been a wonderful knock. Can someone stay around with him and drag this entertainment a bit longer? A possible century perhaps?

FOUR! Wagner comes from round the wicket, bowls a half tracker. Mahmudullah plays the hook shot but could not get the timing. The balls takes the top edge and goes above the keeper who tries a jumping effort to stop the ball but misses.
Around off, blocked from the crease.
A back of length on middle stump moving in for the lefty, watchfully defended on the back foot.
A full length delivery,  around off, Rahman chips it over the bowler. Mustafizur completes a couple before the ball was fielded by mid on.
TOP EDGE, SIX! First of the innings. A length ball on middle, Mustafizur decides to go for broke and swings hard. Gets a top edge but has enough wood on it to clear long leg.
Full and around off, Mustafizur goes back and pushes it uppishly towards the off side.
Full and around off, moving away, Mahmudullah pushes it towards point for a single.
Comes around the wicket and bowls a harmless bouncer outside leg, the Fizz gets across and lets it go.
A bouncer around leg stump, Mustafizur ducks.
Mustafizur Rahman walks in at number 9, replacing Taijul.

OUT! CAUGHT! Number 7 down and Wagner has his third on the trot. Changes the angle and comes from over the wicket but bowls the same line like the previous one. Taijul tried to play the same shot but could not keep it to the ground this time, gets it off his gloves. Tom Latham at silly point takes it comfortably. The match is hastening towards a completion now.
Changes the line on this one, bowls it outside off. Islam jumps and defends it to the ground.
Similar delivery, Islam moves across to play it fine but misses to hit this one.
Short of a length delivery outside leg, Islam moves across and leaves it.
FOUR! A short pitched length outside off, Mahmudullah plays a pull, gets a top edge and the ball goes through mid-wicket for a boundary. 12 runs from this over. Bangladesh are trailing by 51 runs.
A well bowled bouncer for a comeback, pitched on middle, ducked by Mahmudullah.
FOUR! Same line and length outside off and short, a beauty shot by Mahmudullah goes on the back foot and applies a square cut. The ball rockets away behind point.
A short length delivery, well outside off, left alone.
A short ball pitched around off. Slashed on the back foot by Mahmudullah. A good fielding effort at gully.

OVERTHROWS! Full and outside off, Mahmudullah punches it behind point. Comes back for the second but the throw is well wide of the keeper and goes towards mid-wicket. The batsmen run two more. Four runs in total.
Stand-in captain Tim Southee returns. 9-1-35-0 so far.
Pitches this one fuller, Taijul moves across and tries to play it fine but the keeper cuts it off going to his right.
Short ball from round the wicket, Taijul ducks this one.
Taijul Islam walks in at number 8, replacing Mithun.

OUT! Well, caught this time. It is not Mahmudullah but Wagner gets another wicket off a short ball. Bounced in around off, Das goes for the pull but gets a top edge. The ball goes straight to Trent Boult waiting at fine leg, running a bit towards his left and completes the formalities. Innings defeat still on? 63 runs adrift.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Miscommunication between the fielders. A short ball, around off, Mahmudullah goes for the pull but gets a top edge. The ball goes behind short leg and there is a man at square leg too. But neither go for it. The keeper Peter Bocock runs all the way from his position but cannot get there. Wagner is not happy. That should have been taken by square leg.
A short ball, pulled towards long leg for a run.
A bouncer outside leg, ducked under.
A length delivery on middle, watchfully defended on the back foot.
Full and around middle, watchfully blocked out.
A peach of a delivery. Pitched on a fuller length, angling in and changing direction upon pitching around off. Mahmudullah was well beaten while going for a cover drive.
Around middle and leg, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Expertly placed. Outside off, on a length, Mahmudullah steers it behind point for a boundary! Moves to 31.
On a good length around off, defended to the off side.
A bouncer to end the over as well, ducked under.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
A bouncer, outside leg, ducked under.
Liton Das walks in at number 7, replacing Mithun.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mithun has finally fallen to Wagner's short balls. He misses out on a half century. Wagner bowls it around his ribs, Mithun tries to help it round the corner and gets it on his bat but the fielder was placed there right for that shot. Southee at leg gully takes a nice catch near his chest. Bangladesh have lost half of their side. The deficit is still 69.
Wagner is trying the short deliveries here, bowls another half tracker. Mithun ducks and leaves it alone.
Outside off, left alone.
That is a beauty! Full and outside off, Mahmudullah looks to drive but the ball comes in a long way and beats the inside edge!
Around off, defended from the crease.
Full and around middle, flicked through square leg for a couple.
Around middle, helped to the leg side.
Full and just outside off, Mahmudullah defends it back down the pitch.
FOUR! Not a bad shot. On a good length around off, Mithun gets on his toes and helps it above square leg for a boundary! 150 UP FOR BANGLADESH. Trail by 71.
Wagner has been on a short ball barrage, tries to bounce him up but Mithun ducks right in time to let it go over his head.
The batsman stands his crease and plays this short ball really well.
Just like the first delivery and the result is actually the same.
Bowls this one on a good length on middle stump angling away, played towards the cover fielder for no run.
Short ball to start the over, Mithun ducks and leaves it.
Some issue with the ball. The Kiwis are showing it to the umpire. Looks like some thread has come off. It is being cut off.
FOUR! Back of length outside off, Mahmudullah slashes it hard but gets an outside edge. The ball flies over the slips and Mahmudullah gets a boundary in the third man area.
Wide! Another attempted bouncer but Henry applies too much of effort. Pitched on off, the ball goes above the batsman's head and it is a wide.
A well directed bouncer pitched on off, watchfully ducked by Mahmudullah.
Short of good length, pitched around off, defended on the back foot.
FOUR! Lovely wristwork. Full and around middle, Mahmudullah flicks it beautifully through square leg and finds the fence. The skipper moves to 21.
Around middle, the skipper looks to flick but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.

FOUR! A bad delivery outside off, pitched short and Mahmudullah offers a cut shot towards point. Nicholls gets an awkward bounce and misfields it standing at point, and the ball touches the boundary ropes.

DRINKS BREAK. Not a bad passage of play for either side. New Zealand have managed to pick up a wicket while Bangladesh have managed to lose ONLY one wicket. They are trying hard to survive, playing it out passage-wise and seeing off hour by hour. The deficit is still 88 and they do not have much batting left. The barricade of short stuff has started and it will require top concentration to avoid attacking strokes.
Bouncer to end the over, Mithun goes back and leaves it alone.

OUCH! This would hurt. Wagner bowls it short to Mithun, who tries to defend from the back foot but plays it down the wrong line. The bat was nowhere close to the ball and it hits Mithun hard on his ribs.
Short ball on middle, Mithun backs away and tries to play the upper cut but could not connect. The ball misses the edge and goes straight to the keeper.
Outside leg, the skipper hops across and nudges it towards fine leg for a single.
On a good length outside off, angling away, Mahmudullah feels for it but misses.
FOUR! Fine shot. A short ball, around off, Mahmudullah pulls it through square leg and finds the boundary.
Short leg comes into play. Tom Latham it is under the lid.

FOUR! Back of length, pitched on middle leg, swinging in for Mithun, he plays a loose flick shot of his pads and the ball flies through an empty mid-wicket region. The ball touches the boundary ropes.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fullish in length, driven straight to mid on.
Short of a good length, swings in the air but goes out after pitching on off stump. Mithun hops across to defend but gets a leading edge which does not carry to cover.
A bouncer and around off, Mithun ducks. The ball swerves a long way after pitching.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
This one was bowled outside leg, the batsman leaves it alone.
FOUR! Back of a length delivery outside leg, Mahmudullah plays it fine off his pads. The ball rolls away to the vacant fine leg region. Boundary signalled.
Mahmudullah tries to hook on this short delivery but could not connect and it misses the top edge. The ball goes straight to the keeper who appeals but the umpire straightaway denies.
FOUR! Pitched short outside leg, Mahmudullah plays the pull shot with perfect timing and the ball races away to the fence at the backward square leg region.
Goes short this time, Mahmudullah ducks and it goes straight to the keeper.
Starts his over for the day with a back of a length delivery at the batsman's ribs, defended off the back foot.
Neil Wagner into the attack too. Southee ringing in the changes. 4-2-8-0 so far.
Length ball on off, sliding in for Mithun. He was trying flick it on the back foot but the ball hits him on his thigh pad, just a routine appeal from behind the stumps.
Outside off, back of length, left alone.
A length ball around off, watchfully shown the full bat by Mithun, straight to mid on.
On a good length outside off, defended from the crease.
A back of length this time, pitched around off and the ball swinging in, defended with ease by Mithun.
Henry starts with a short of length ball, easily defended on the back foot.
Matt Henry into the attack as well. 4-2-17-1 so far.
Fuller delivery outside off, watchfully defended off the front foot.
Strays on the pads, Mithun clips it to the square leg region for a single.
Just like the second delivery, plays a full ball which takes the inside edge onto his pads.
Full ball outside off, left alone.
Similar length on the pads, Mithun tries to defend but gets the inside edge on his pads & it rolls to the bowler.
Full ball to start the over, driven straight to mid off.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
Another short ball, around off, Mahmudullah sways away from the line.
Around middle and off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and just around off, swinging in slightly, watchfully defended back to the bowler.
Around off, angling away, shouldered arms to.
Full and around middle and leg, watchfully defended.
Outside off, length ball, a good leave by Mithun.
Full length around off, shown full face of the bat, straight to mid off.
Outside off, punched through point for a couple.
Wide! A bouncer pitched on middle, ducked by Mithun. Wide given by the umpire.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Change in line, fuller length angling in for Mithun. Defends it under his eyes.
Length ball, outside off, left alone.
Around middle and off, pushed back to the bowler. Successful over for Boult.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A bouncer around middle and leg, ducked under.
Outside off, quietly left alone this time.
On a good length outside off, Mahmudullah pushes at it away from his body and gets an outside edge. Lands short of gully.
Skipper Mahmudullah walks in at number 6, replacing Sarkar.

OUT! Edged and taken! There goes the first wicket of the day. Boult has not taken long to strike. What a delivery to get Sarkar. He was having trouble to play his outswingers and gets caught on this one. Coming to the ball, it was pitched back off a length. Sarkar tries to poke at it, but the ball takes the outside edge and goes straight to Taylor at first slip who takes it easily. Sarkar doesn't make much use of the opportunities given to him, first a run out miss and then a dropped catch. Bangladesh are still trailing by 109 runs. NZ need 6 more wickets to end this match.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! Nice shot. Full and around off, Mithun walks into the shot and drives it down the ground. Mid on gives it a chase but comes second best.
Similar ball, shouldered arms to again.
On a good length outside off, angling away, left alone.
Around off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, swinging away, Mithun looks to drive but gets an outside edge which lands in front of gully.
Colin de Grandhomme into the attack now. 2-0-3-0 so far.
Back off a length delivery, defended off the back foot.
The batsman got beaten on this delivery as he was playing down the wrong line. The ball was pitched short and shaped away a little, missed Sarkar's outside edge and went straight to the keeper.
Full ball outside off, driven through the cover region. Both the cover fielders give it a chase and pull it off just inside the boundary. 3 runs completed.
Short ball on his ribs, Mithun does well to evade this one.
Piched this one short, Mithun ducks down as it was near his head. The keeper takes it above his head.
On a length outside off, moving away, dabbed to gully.

A dropped chance! Hard chance, but will go down as dropped by Southee. Full toss on middle and leg, swinging in for Sarkar, Soumya wanted to play with the full face but the bat turns in his hand and Southee has a tough chance in his followthrough. He gives a diving effort but unfortunately for him, the ball doesn't stick in his left hand.

FOUR! Back of length outside off and moving away, Sarkar had his eye lit up for that and and slashes it hard in the air, the ball flies above gully and gets to the boundary ropes. Brings up the 50-run stand between the pair. That will be a sigh of relief for Bangladesh.
Slightly fuller in length on off, almost a yorker, Sarkar lets the ball come to him and watchfully nudges to point for a double. And that is 100 up for Bangladesh on scoreboard.
Short of good length around off, with hint of away swing, Sarkar shoulders his arms.
Short and outside off, extra bounce, fended towards point for a single.
Around middle, defended to the leg side.

That's an outstanding delivery. Boult bowls it on a length angling away to the batsman, Sarkar is beaten up by the movement. He tries to defend it, but gets an outside edge which falls just short of Taylor at second slip.
Fuller ball on off stump line, defended by Sarkar.
Short of a length delivery, beats the outside edge just by an inch.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Poor stuff from the substitute keeper. Sarkar was gone for all money. Outside off, Mithun punched it through the covers and started into a jog. He was accompanied by Sarkar and the duo calmly completed a couple and also turned blind for the third. There was no urgency in the running and the throw came in at a nice height to the keeper Peter Bocock with Soumya halfway down. However, the keeper fumbles it.
Changes the angle on this one, comes from round the wicket, pulls the length short. Mithun goes on the back foot to defend it.
Back of a length delivery just outside off, Mithun defends it to the covers.
Wide outside off, left alone by Sarkar, just too wide by Southee for the batsman to make any contact.
A beautiful drive straight to mid off, pitched on off, length ball moving away, Sarkar plays with a full face, straight to mid off. Some batting knocking routine.
Short of good length on leg, defended on the back foot by Sarkar.
Shorter length pitched on middle-leg, watchfully defended by Sarkar under his eyes.
Full and outside off again, Soumya drives this loosely, in the air, but just eludes the man at short cover!
FOUR! SUBLIME! Full and outside off, Sarkar drives this straight back past the non-striker, beating mid off with consummate ease!
Dot ball to end the over. Pitching inside the tram line. Mithun goes forward to attempt the drive, but pulls away at the end.
Similar delivery, similar result. Mithun leaves this one.
Fuller in length this time, left alone to the keeper.
Another short ball, defended watchfully off the back foot.
Short ball on the body, Mithun defends it off the back foot.
Full ball angling away, Mithun shoulders arms.
Length ball on middle-leg, showed full face of the bat, straight to the bowler.
Shorter in length, Southee was looking for a bouncer, pitched on off, ducked by Sarkar.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length ball on off, moving away, nicely shouldered arms to that.
FOUR! A juicy volley on off, lofted over covers by Sarkar for a boundary. That was a positive shot by Sarkar, showing character for the survival for this Test.
Way outside off by Southee, left alone by Sarkar.

WIDE! Superb keeping though. A short ball, banged in the middle of the pitch, Sarkar ducks but the ball keeps on rising. Substitute keeper, Peter Bocock, leaps full stretch and takes it with one glove.
FOUR LEG BYES! Strays in line, bowls it around leg, Mithun gets across and looks to flick but misses. The ball though kisses his thigh pads and goes past the diving keeper to the fine leg fence.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side, helped wide of mid on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, Sarkar feels for it but misses.
Trent Boult to bowl from the other end.
Change of line this time, length ball on leg. Flicked for a single towards mid-wicket by Sarkar.
Shorter in length, pitched outside off, angled away for the lefty, left alone.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Soumya.
Full length on off, easily defended by Soumya.
Outside off, gentle tempter, fuller in length, left alone.
Full and outside off, Sarkar pushes at this a bit loosely, cannot quite control it and just about eludes the diving short cover fielder. Cover mops it up.
Okay. We are all ready for the game to begin. Tim Southee to start off proceedings to Soumya Sarkar. Mohammad Mithun is at the other end. Here we go...
WEATHER - It is pretty overcast with a slight chance of rain. Hopefully, it does not rain.

1 session? 2 sessions? Whole day? How long will the game last? With 7 wickets in hand, probably you back the Kiwis to finish this off in a session. Can Bangladesh offer some resistance? Hello and a warm welcome to the final day's play of the second Test between New Zealand and Bangladesh in Wellington.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...

Thus, the Test which was looking like a hopeless one has suddenly turned into one which could surely have a result. The Kiwis are sure favourites with just 7 wickets to take and a lead of 141 yet to boot. The best the Tigers can hope for is to salvage a draw. They would not mind some help from the fickle weather of Wellington but the forecast is decent for Tuesday. An exciting finish is expected for sure, will the home side wrap up the game and take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series or will Bangladesh manage to take it to the final Test with the series still alive? Join us at 1030 local (2130 GMT, Monday night) to find out. Till then, take care and cheers!

Ross Taylor says that he is really happy with his hundred and more so because it was a difficult pitch to bat on where any  particular ball could get your wicket. He says that he was lucky to survive the morning and that the heavy roller they used was helpful in the end. When asked about the speed with which they batted today, he informs us that it had to be done especially since it was a 3-day Test. Ross tells us that their plan was to attack the seamers as they had only 3 in their side. They initially wanted a lead of 100 just to get a result in the game but feels that this was a bonus. Gets emotional when asked about going past Crowe's 17 centuries and says it would have made him proud. He signs off by saying that they want to pick up early wickets on Day 5 and they don't mind chasing 40-50 runs in the final innings if that happens. Finally, he also adds that this surface is still less green than the Hobart one that he played on in the past.

The day belonged to Ross Taylor. He made his 18th ton in Tests, going past his role model and former hero, Martin Crowe. He converted it into a double century and along with the company of Williamson and Nicholls, he set a lead of 221 runs over the away side. Trent Boult started off the second innings on a super note with a second-ball wicket of Tamim Iqbal. That rocked the visitors and they lost 2 more wickets until Stumps. Mohammad Mithun and Soumya Sarkar are unbeaten right now and will look to come on Day 5 and bat a long time if their team is to have any hopes. Just before you go though, a special interview comes your way!

What a Test match we have witnessed here at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. 2 days washed out, 2 days of super-fast Test cricket. Day 4 started with the hosts, New Zealand starting at 38/2 in pursuit of Bangladesh's 211. They provided a batting masterclass as they attacked and attacked adding 394 runs to their overnight score, 200 of which came of Ross Taylor's bat. They ended up declaring with a lot of time left in the final session and they even managed to pick up 3 wickets in the 2nd innings of the visitors. The lead is still 141 and the hosts will be more than hopeful of claiming a victory on Day 5 provided the weather remains good like it did on Day 4 all day long!

OUT! Three down! Henry has done it courtesy of the steep bounce! Neil Wagner had mentioned about it yesterday and a pace compatriot has done the job today. A short length ball on the leg stump line, Shadman looks to pull it but the extra bounce means the ball takes a faint top edge and goes through to Watling who takes a decent but easy catch. The umpire raises the finger after the bowler appeals and a dejected Islam has to walk off after a good-looking 29. The Kiwis are on a roll here.
